utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Karadzic. Good morning, Mr. Witness. Mr. Karadzic, you will have 40 minutes to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Do I start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to lose as little time as possible, can we have 65 ter 09784, page 2. I just wanted to complete this incident in Safeta Hadzica. May I ask you -- may I ask all the parties, towards the tracks, regarding the tracks, it's underneath these elements: "According to the marks, it was established that all the projectiles from an unidentified weapon to date were fired from the west, which corresponds to the aggressor positions of the rebel Bosnian Serbs in the Ilidza area."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, you're saying that you don't know what was the weapon the projectiles were fired from, which, by the way, don't exist, armoured projectiles. The only thing that is established is that they were fired from Serbian positions. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see -- it's true that at that point in time, I didn't know the weapon from which they were fired. It does not say in the report that it was fired definitely from those positions, but it says that they were fired from the direction of the west. The projectile exists. It was photographed, and I assume that the photograph of the projectile is part of the photo documentation. It's a projectile that I saw with my own eyes, and I copied from it -- or recorded the markings on it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We must intervene for the transcript. A part of the witness's answer stating it was not decisively established was not recorded. Did you say that it was not decisively recorded?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was not written in the record that it was decisively fired from that direction, but there is a description that that direction corresponds to the position of the aggressor forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about that stretch of space between the location of the incident and the position of the aggressor forces; was there any soldier -- were there any soldiers there? There is a territory there that is controlled by the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army, and then at the end of that, there is no-man's land, and then there is the Serbian line there and then the Serbian territory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that there were lines there held by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, I don't know where those lines were and what their disposition were. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now -- I think that this is the same number. Just one moment. Yes, yes. Can we now get page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who inspected the material here, which expert was it? Was it Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see who examined the objects. All I can see is the signature of the person who I know. I can see his first and last name. I know that he was the chief of the department. I don't know who did the actual inspection. Actually, this is a different organisational unit, so I'm not sure who would have been responsible for that, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, all right. We will come to that. Is it true that in this report, we are talking about an impact projectile of 88 millimetres in calibre?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here. I don't know where the object was found, but it does say that it's a contact fuse, high-explosive projectile, of 88 millimetres in calibre. I don't see from which event that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But did you write that it was a 90-millimetre calibre projectile?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report, it does say "90-millimetre projectile," but I don't know whether this particular report refers to the same projectile that I saw.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the page before. Page 11, can we see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this, this part here, the first page, and if you can tell us how things stand. Does this refer to the Safeta Hadzica incident, this incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the introduction, yes, it refers to that incident, the shelling of Safeta Hadzica Street in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has this document been tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it it has been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It was admitted under seal, but we'll have a public version very soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I would now like to deal with the incident -- or, rather, the shelling -- the incident related to the radio/television building. Did you take part in that investigation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For a major part of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you conclude that the television was hit with a modified air-bomb?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to underline that I never concluded anything. I was just making a report about things that pertain to my part of the investigation, as some information was told to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the conclusion of the Military Observers of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But they were present during the on-scene investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They arrived together with -- yes, they were present at the scene, and they were observing while the team was working. They were there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter 9825, page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This entire team, was it present on the scene, and did they all take part in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, yes, the team came on the scene. They did carry out investigative actions in relation to this incident. I don't know whether all of them remained right until the end. I can say, about myself, that at one point I did leave the scene and go to another investigation which occurred in the immediate vicinity. A modified air-bomb hit an apartment in a high-rise building. I don't know whether all the other crew members or team members stayed on the scene until the investigation was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which incident are you talking about, the one that you left for? Is that the Cetinjska Street? Which incident did you go to from this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a high-rise building at Alipasino Polje. I don't know what the name of the street at the time was, but I will try to find it in my report. It could have been Geteova Street or Cetinjska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll leave that for now. Can we have page 2 of this document, please. This is your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just look at the signature at the end?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You have it in your papers.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm trying to find it. Yes, I do have that report in front of me. The report was written by my colleague. I didn't sign it. I don't know right now why I didn't sign it then. Probably because I went to the scene of this other incident. I really cannot remember now why that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But they typed your name, and he just initialled it, and you two are mentioned as the persons who drafted the report.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can completely stand by what is written in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Does it not say in this paragraph that around 9.00, between -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which page you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the first paragraph on page 2.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "Just in front of the entrance to the open area on the ground floor, inflicting extensive material damage to the building ..." And then in the second paragraph, it says in line 4: "... on the part where the western and the northern part of the building meet, next to the wall of studio C west is the center of the explosion." Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain how this bomb managed to get right to the base of Studio C without hitting the upper sections of Studio C?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain that. I'm not that versed in that kind of thing, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 09851. That is the page number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that: Have we admitted this one, 65 ter 9825?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it was admitted. Yes, thank you. It was a part of your additional disclosure or the additional 65 ter numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: It was indicated as an additional document. We didn't use it with the witness. We're happy for it to be admitted now, but I would note that this incident has been dropped from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's a removed one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we thought that, since it was in the additional notice, I thought it was one of the associated exhibits. But it was not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the thing is that it hasn't been admitted yet. Do you like to tender it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes, because these answers need to be connected to that particular part. This is in the statement. The statement is part of the case file, and that is that spice to make the stew thicker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thanks for the clarification. We'll strike out that exhibit from the Prosecution's exhibit. Instead, we'll admit it as a Defence exhibit, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D868, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I would like you to produce a public version with proper redactions. We'll give another number for a public version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be Exhibit D869.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that in this case, the round ricochetted? How did it leave the normal trajectory? How did it end up outside any possible trajectory?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many times I need to tell you: I really don't know, and I did not meddle in that. With all the experts in that field of work who were present on the scene, I did not need to get involved in that, and I cannot explain things that I am not an expert for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that's in the report that you stand by. Did anyone tell you anything about the path of this projectile, out of the 11 people who are on the list?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every report, not only on this incident, but in every report we made, there is some preliminary data that we received from experts and people who specialise in these things. This report is no exception. All this data needs to be viewed as preliminary, and all this data needs to be confirmed after expert examination and reports. And in every report, you will see a preliminary indication from where the projectile came, but there is no conclusion that that was, indeed, so. That's what experts are for. That's why they come onto the scene.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 65 ter 09851, page 3. The lower photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this part of the file, this file?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the captions below the photographs, and from the upper photograph, I recognise the radio/television building. I suppose it relates to this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it follow from this that the projectile ricochetted from here and that possibility is not accounted for in your report?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was a possibility or not, whether it ricochetted or not. In the caption below the photograph, it says the projectile ricochetted from there. I don't know. You have to ask the experts who worked with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this is part -- an integral part of the document. Why was it not said in the report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To go on with such questions is a waste of time. We have heard already that the witness is not an expert so as to be able to answer such questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not asking the witness how it ricochetted, but why it's not in the report that he stands by and that he signed. If he can't answer even that question, fine, but the question is why such a major fact is not mentioned in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there any position taken on the azimuth --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Can you answer the question --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to repeat what I've already said. Regarding the direction of fire, this is the information we received from the experts on the scene. Now, why there is no other comment about this than in the photo file, the photo file is done by a completely different person who has the job title of scene-of-crime officer. This is his document, and I cannot comment on it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just answer one question. Does that mean that nobody made you aware of the fact that the entire team believed there was a ricochet?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me, and I don't know how important that would be at that time on the scene. Until all our opinions are confirmed by expertise, we could have thought or commented whatever we liked, but final conclusions are made through expertise and expert examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the direction from which the projectile was fired, let's look -- this is probably already an exhibit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D526, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to your report. That's 9825, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You put in your report that it was a rocket projectile fired from the north-west azimuth, 288 degrees, which corresponds to the aggressor-held settlement Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's in the report. And let me emphasise I did not write this report. I just stand behind it. That's what's written in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it completed and submitted on the 28th of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when -- on what day my colleague submitted this report. That was his job. I cannot recall and I don't know whether he did it the same day or the next day. I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, who from the team gave you this figure, 288 degrees? Who determined the azimuth?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're again asking me to recall such details after so much time. Moreover, you can see in the report there were several people who deal with these things; our experts from the police, mainly. And you're asking me to remember that now. Even if I really wanted to, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any other topic to cover with this witness, other than this one?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. I just have one more question on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then I have to say that it is not a wise use of time, given that this incident is a removed one, removed from the indictment, and the Prosecution didn't lead any evidence in relation to this in relation to this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it's in the statement, in his statement, together with other statements, and it makes the statement more dangerous to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: That's incorrect, it's not in the statement. It's recorded in the statement that he attended this investigation, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: -- that's all. And it was only by way of context, because he investigated another incident that day, as recorded in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then we'll move on to the next incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that you participated in the investigation of the incident in Geteova Street, number 5, which used to be called Cetinjska Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it's about the high-rise and the modified air-bomb, I can find it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 65 ter 9828. 19828, without broadcasting, or 1D9828.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it for this incident that you left the incident related to the television building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that the crime scene was not secured, but it had not been altered. Based on what did you conclude that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I, indeed, did write that the crime scene was not secured, but it wasn't altered, compared to the reported incident, because there was nothing to alter. It wasn't possible to alter anything from the moment when we were told of the incident and the moment we arrived, because we came so quickly, and the crime scene was such that it couldn't be altered in any major way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you state that on the eighth floor, a projectile of great destructive power exploded, where it impacted, and the chambers of three rocket motors were found and submitted for expertise?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the last paragraph but one: "Based on the situation as found and the traces found after the impact of the projectile, it was determined that it was fired from the direction south-south-west, azimuth" such and such, "which corresponds to positions in the area of Ilidza."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden, can I get your assistance once again. As to the status of this incident, this is not included in the indictment, and you didn't lead any evidence in relation to this as an unscheduled incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: No, that's not correct, Your Honour. This does appear in the witness's statement at paragraph 22 and 23, and one of the associated exhibits, which is on the screen before us, was admitted through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this has been admitted, this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: This report is an associated exhibit, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think this was one of the associated exhibits tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Sir, I think the one we see on our screen is a duplicate of the associated exhibit, which is 65 ter 14397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 14 -- there was the origin of my mistake. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why do you have such a big error margin here, 25 degrees?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the conclusion here again that it came from Serbian aggressor positions or that it's in that direction?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the direction west-south-west was established, and it corresponds to positions in the area of Ilidza, and it's written in the report that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are we then to consider it was determined that it came from those positions, or is it again in the conditional, like in previous cases?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's determined or established at the moment when it is established by experts in the area. And from that moment only, we can consider it as a fact, an established fact, like in all the previous incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this does not suffice for us to say that it was fired by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're trying to say with that question. In any case, this is certainly part of the whole material that was gathered at the scene, and you can treat it as best you think fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You claimed, in an interview with the Defence, that these kind of data was always provided exclusively by ballistics experts.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody from that area of expertise. Or if a ballistic expert was not available, then a scene-of-crime officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From that list on the paper, can you indicate, by number, the person who would have been qualified to provide this information?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can probably see from the list that it's an incident that occurred 12 or 13 years ago and that there were several members of the team who were able to provide this piece of information. I can only tell you that I can't remember the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Are we looking at the correct translation? I'm not sure whether those two documents are identical ones.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cetinjska, Geteova Street, I think. Iset Alihodzic, there's a name. [In English] "... information gathered at the site revealed that --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, it's for you to make sure that we are seeing the correct documents. The English translation seems to be a different one. I don't see such --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These markings are on the next page. It's the same document, but in English it probably straddles onto the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The next page has -- we have to go back to the original 65 ter document, 14397. That may be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that: Witness, were there any troops of the BH Army or anything from the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the place of impact, the location of the incident.

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a residential high-rise. It contained apartments of army members, perhaps, but I didn't see any premises where army troops could have been stationed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it now the right page, Your Excellency?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I see the whole page, which you couldn't see with this previous one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't know what the status of this document is. I think it's an exhibit. Can we now get 1D2691. 1D2691.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are not sure whether the accused said it can or cannot be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll not broadcast this. Did you say we can't broadcast?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, we can, we can, we can. It has nothing to do with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a combat report of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the 1st Corps, dated the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I only agree that that is what is written there. Whether that is so or not, I don't know, but I do confirm that that is what is written there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

Do you agree that that day, from that location, the body of a fighter was pulled out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I don't know if the accused is going to be much longer with this document, but there is a translation available in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: We haven't had a chance to look at the translation yet. When we do, we might be able to respond. At this stage, no objection, but I can get back to you very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D02175, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D2719. 2719.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

It can be seen right beneath the crown of the trees. You have zoomed in so that we can see the rest of that building. That is the part of the television building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I assume that that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]

utterances.text: No. It's time to wrap up your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I would like you to understand that nothing was directed against you or against your service. All we are seeking to do is to establish the facts. Thank you. Thank you, yes, thank you for your co-operation, but I must say for the transcript that we did not manage to cover Markale 2, which was also part of your job. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ485 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at that scene with my colleagues, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and I wish you a safe trip home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber sees no basis to admit the Defence Exhibit D872, since the witness was not able to confirm the location. And the Chamber is of the view, Mr. Karadzic, that the time that was allowed to you to cross-examine this witness, i.e., three and a half hours, is more than sufficient, and it is not acceptable that you are complaining of shortage of time, having wasted a lot of time. The Chamber will come to that issue later on. Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then it concludes your evidence, Mr. Witness. I'd like to thank you, on behalf of the Tribunal and the Bench, to come to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. But stay there. We'll have a short break in order to accommodate the logistics. We'll break for --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I -- may I say: When are we -- I would like, before the next witness, just to say one word about this circumstance, this circumstance of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you will have that opportunity when we resume. We'll break for 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It would be fair and even essential for me to present to the Chamber my position on the matter of time. First of all, it's a fact that the Prosecution is introducing, through these witnesses, let's say through the witness who's coming next -- the statement of the next witness mentions 19 incidents. They're not all in the indictment, but 19 incidents are referred to, and the statement contains 80 references. While my team is studying the witness statements, they found 336 additional references. If the Prosecution were to add 17 new incidents, and they do that in order to establish a pattern, and I have to deal with all of these 17 incidents in order to deal with the credibility of the witness and the credibility of that method. And not only that but I also am doing that by means of looking at these 336 references. If I go incident by incident with the witness that's coming, and also with the previous witness, one can conclude that I am getting 30 to 40 minutes per incident, based on the time allotted to me. And, believe me, in your countries, you would be spending at least five or six days dealing with each of these incidents. We also have a very large problem here of incompetent witnesses. We're talking about counter-sabotage protection. Nobody wanted to discuss that except for Mr. Sabljica. 166 didn't speak of that or Mr. Suljevic either. We cannot decide who is responsible for what, who is standing behind what in these reports. They, themselves, are aware and admit that these reports wouldn't be much good before our courts either. Nevertheless, they appear before this Tribunal. I was watching, in other cases, how much tiny elements were taken into account, and major official reports of UN observers and so on were not taken into account and people were convicted because this system of ours is different from this one that is being applied here, and the accused were not able to put up a suitable defence. If I enter into that pattern where there is no chance of me defending myself, then these whole proceedings have no sense any longer. Witnesses are like fish. They wriggle out of one's grasp. You cannot keep them to their words. You cannot find out who is the author of the investigation materials, author of reports. So with all due respect, I kindly ask you for the indulgence of all parties, particularly the witness -- that I'm in a very difficult position, I'm being pulled in all directions, I'm not getting enough time. And as Mr. Hayden and Mr. Tieger said a few days ago, time is of the essence. Actually, time is not of the essence; truth is of the essence. And I do not wish these proceedings to be made invalid because of a number of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me just note quickly, Your Honour, that that is a deflection from the issue at hand, which is the accused's use of the time allotted, which has repeatedly demonstrated that he's purposefully not using the time allotted to elicit from the witnesses what they know or saw or heard, or challenge those observations or information, but instead to use them as a pretext to argue his case in other ways or submit to them documentation about which they cannot possibly shed light. In addition, as we saw yesterday, he repeatedly refuses to put his case to the witnesses in a purposeful manner, instead focusing on matters on the periphery, and only when pressed by the Court, reluctantly once, then move forward to try to put his case to the witness in a manner that would allow the cross-examination to proceed efficiently, and also demonstrated that the time allotted was more than ample and that the Court had been extraordinarily patient with that cross-examination as well as previous cross-examinations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure it is for Mr. Tieger or Mr. Gaynor to respond to this, but is the next witness a sort of ballistic expert who will give his -- give evidence as to the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. He worked for the KDZ of the RBiH MUP, which is the Counter-Sabotage Protection Unit, so his evidence does concern ballistics. He's a fact witness, not an expert witness, but it does concern --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is his evidence of the limited nature as the previous one, KDZ485?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would say that this witness was more involved in a more complex set of determinations, such as the angle of impact -- the angle of the projectile upon impact and the direction of fire, and so he would -- the nature of his evidence would be a little more complex than the evidence of the witness that we've just heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, the position is, in effect, as Mr. Tieger has put it: The reality is cross-examination is a mixture of an art and a science, and where you elect to represent yourself, you take upon the burdens of discharging both the art and the science of cross-examination. But as I've said before, we recognise that you're not practiced in it, and it may be unfair for me - and I speak for myself personally, with some 30 years of cross-examining people both from a defence and a prosecution perspective - to expect you to be able to adopt all the techniques and nuances. But what you are singularly failing to do, it seems to me, is to do that which Mr. Tieger advances, which is to put your case to the witness. You do not have to, in cross-examination, go through the whole of a witness's statement. What matters is that you put the essence of the case where the witness's statement touches and concerns the matters which are against you on the indictment. Those are the things that the Court is going to be looking at in the long run, and you can be sure that peripheral matters, which do not assist the Court, are not going to be held to your prejudice. What we would very much like you to do with this witness is to try and concentrate on putting your case. If, as has been the case with virtually every witness we've had, you put your case and we feel that you are making progress, then time may be extended. There's no promises. But time is, to some extent, of the essence, because part of the fair trial matrix is an expeditious trial, and where a trial is not expeditious, much is lost; not simply for the trial, itself, in terms of an administrative beast, but for you, in terms of concentrating on what really matters. And that's what touches and concerns us, what really matters. So take what I say to heart. And you may recall, when we first started this case, I gave what was reported in the press as a short tutorial on cross-examination. I'm perfectly prepared to repeat that at some point in the future, but I shouldn't have to do that, because you have experienced lawyers around you whose views you should be taking and adopting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the Chamber is not minded to change the time allotted to you, which the Chamber finds sufficient time for you to cover all the incidents to be covered by this witness. And for the scheduling matter, we decided to sit until 4.00 this afternoon, thanks to the indulgence of the interpreters and court reporters. I appreciate it, again. And the breaks will be planned, and it will be known to the parties in due course. That said, we'll bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, could you state your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Emir Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You've previously testified in the trials of Dragomir Milosevic and Momcilo Perisic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You've previously given statements to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You've had an opportunity to review an amalgamated statement containing relevant extracts from your testimonies and from your statements; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask for 65 ter 22270, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: On the screen in front of you, Mr. Turkusic, do you see an electronic version of the first page of your amalgamated statement?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I understand that you wish to make one correction to a typographical error in the statement on page 5. I'll note it for the record. At line 5, the word "Kraljevo" should read "Krusik Valjevo"; is that correct, Mr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Correct. It's an abbreviation that means the place where the fuse of the shell was produced and written. In Cyrillic, that abbreviation means "Krusik Valjevo," not "Kraljevo."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Subject to that correction, does the amalgamated statement accurately reflect the evidence you have previously given? And if you were questioned on the same topics today, would you provide the same information to the Court?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, in full.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I seek admission of the amalgamated statement, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1924, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll now read a summary of the evidence of the witness. Mr. Turkusic was a member of the Counter-Sabotage Protection Unit of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which is the RBiH MUP KDZ. The witness and his team conducted numerous ballistic investigations into shelling incidents in Sarajevo. His statement concerns the role of the RBiH MUP KDZ in shelling investigations, the method of determining the direction of fire of a mortar round, the accuracy of mortars, and the nature of modified air-bombs. He discusses in detail investigative documentation relating to 16 shelling incidents, and comments, in particular, on the nature of the projectiles which detonated and the direction of fire. He also discusses a shelling incident on the 28th of August, 1995, in which a 120-millimetre mortar shell detonated outside the entrance to the city market, Scheduled Incident G19. Forty-three people were killed and seventy-five injured. Mr. Turkusic, who arrived at the incident site shortly after the detonation of the projectile, describes the huge pools of blood and severed body parts which he saw. He also describes the atmosphere of panic and fear at the incident site. Mr. Turkusic notes the stabiliser of the projectile bore markings which indicated that it was manufactured in Valjevo, Serbia, in 1993. He explains that the 120-millimetre mortar round is an anti-personnel projectile, designed to destroy manpower. It sprays its shrapnel in a horizontal fashion close to the ground. Mr. Turkusic discusses the minimal angle of descent and the direction of fire of the projectile. That ends the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, is it correct that you hold a PhD in Chemistry?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, within the RBiH MUP KDZ, could you describe your specific duties during your work there in 1994 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: My duties, like those of all the investigating team in the KDZ Unit, were, in every case of shelling that incurred fatalities or wounds, as well as major material damage, to investigate, in the greatest possible detail, and document that as exhibits, as evidence, that we deposited in our archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did -- your specific area of expertise within the KDZ, did that include the field of pyrotechnics?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was part of my appointment by the minister in a decision where I was appointed inspector for the application of counter-sabotage measures, including pyrotechnics.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you explain, in brief terms, what pyrotechnics is?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Pyrotechnics is just one of the areas of chemistry, and it studies reactions that are ultra-high velocity chemistry reactions that release, in a very short time, a large amount of energy. Pyrotechnics include the most innocuous devices, like firecrackers, up to the highly- sophisticated devices for destruction and anything that initiates explosions in any of the forms to cause major devastation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In your statement, at page 5, when you describe your work at the KDZ, you said you had access to books and manuals. What did you mean by that? What kinds of books and manuals did you have at the KDZ?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Pyrotechnics as an area of chemistry, is familiar to every chemical engineer. It's just one of the areas that studies ultra-high velocity chemical reactions. When we needed to concentrate specifically on that area, I, like all members of the KDZ, our entire team, intensively used very extensive and high-quality literature that we had available to us relating to the area of wartime legal devices, including pyrotechnical devices, and within a very short time we became very well-versed in that area. Our work was closely tied with the work of engineers employed in the military industry that was very developed in Sarajevo. And in co-operation with them, we rounded off and constantly added to the knowledge of our team that was multi-disciplinary and included all the specialties and areas of expertise needed for our specific work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the subject of books and manuals, did -- the books you had access to, did that include books relating to munitions, firing tables, that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Precisely. We had firing tables for all projectiles that were landing on Sarajevo, mortar and artillery, as well as books that dealt with the construction and the technical specifications of all lethal assets, and all the details related to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to turn now to the subject of modified air-bombs, which you describe in your statement. Now, did you, while you were at the KDZ, have the opportunity to inspect the remnants of modified air-bombs which had exploded?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: There was a period where there were a large number of attacks with those modified air-bombs, and the remaining fragments were conscientiously collected by us, documented, recorded in protocols, at least every one that we considered relevant for our archives, whereas the remaining fragments of those rocket engines and shrapnel and parts of the construction of these air-bombs was deposited in a room that, with time, became overloaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: At page 6 of your statement, you state that modified air-bombs were not high-precision weapons. You give a couple of reasons for that, briefly, including references to the symmetry of the charges and other matters. I want to explore that with you, and I'd like you to identify the factors which are relevant to determining whether a modified air-bomb is a precision weapon.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: An air-bomb, used in the way it was developed and designed, when it's released from a plane, is relatively precise. However, in a different combination, when an air-bomb as an explosive device is used by launching it with rocket engines that, by establishment, are not prepared for launching such a bomb at relatively close range, devices were made which, by the way they were improvised and made, could in no way be precise. First of all, these rocket engines, in their chain of activation, have two chemical steps in which there can be a deviation in the simultaneity of the ignition of all engines. The second reason is the following: It is absolutely impossible, with the improvised combination of an air-bomb with rocket engines, to achieve sufficient precision in the parallel nature of the rocket axis -- of the rocket motors with the axis of the air-bomb. Every deviation in angle, including just 1 to 2 degrees, considering the sophisticated nature of such a device, would lead, and certainly led, to imprecision in direction. That is to say, the air-bomb rotated in air due to one of the rotation impulses caused by one or more engines, and these impulses could be superimposed or increase each other, and the result is imprecision. For instance, two air-bombs fired one after another will certainly not land in the same place. The third reason that could lead to imprecision is the simultaneity of ignition of all the four engines and the same duration of work of all the four engines. Both errors lead to a delay in impulse after firing, and the direction of the air-bomb deviates from the direction in which it was launched by the launching pad. And, excuse me, there's one important reason more. A modified device, because that's the only way you can call it - it's a combination of an air-bomb with rocket engines put together by improvisation - is absolutely not aerodynamic. Any body flying through the air, if it's not aerodynamic in shape, is prone to change direction due to high resistance to air. I was not an eye-witness, but there were many eye-witnesses who said they saw this device flying through the air slowly, causing a lot of noise, and that was at the moment when the rocket engine stopped working, and all that speaks about the fact that these modified air-bombs were not aerodynamic at all. And that's another reason for their imprecision.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, what effect would a slight inaccuracy in attaching one of the rocket motors to the air-bomb have on the direction of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Imprecision in mounting these air-bombs, the fact that it's impossible to make all these rocket engines parallel, which would guarantee a proper straight direction, and the imprecision of the bomb, itself, makes these devices completely imprecise, in terms of a clearly-defined target. However, if you define a very large target, because accuracy is relative to size, if you define the target as the city of Sarajevo, then you can say that these air-bombs had the intention to kill, devastate, and destroy. And if you define them as such and the target as such, then you could say they're absolutely precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just going back to the technical point of ignition of the rocket motors, could you explain what effect a slightly non-simultaneous ignition of one or more of the rocket motors would have on the direction of the projectile? By "slight," I'm talking a few nanoseconds or of that order.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, the main premise in launching is that all four rocket engines would activate at the same time. That means with an error margin close to zero in time, and that is achieved at the level of the electronic impulse that reaches the fuse. However, with that electronic impulse, there are two chemical chains that could introduce a margin of error in time. The second engine could react faster. That's the activation of fuse and the activation of fuel in every rocket engine. That inaccuracy, which could be cumulative, could lead to one or more engines activating faster and working shorter, or activating later and working longer than others which, as the device leaves the launching pad, would immediately lead to a deviation impulse, because that modified device is one body, practically. Any impact of force anywhere on the body will, according to the law on maintenance of movement, lead to deviation from the course defined by the direction of the launching ramp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: While you were working for the ABiH, and later for the KDZ, did you ever encounter credible information that Bosnian Government forces were using modified air-bombs?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to the Markale 2 incident. You say in your statement that you arrived in the vicinity of the Markale Market shortly after the detonation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe the circumstances which led you to being in the area at that time.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: By analysing the events after I and colleagues arrived there, it was possible to conclude that we did not hear the explosion, itself, because we were deep inside the building of the Ministry of the Interior, on a side where noise reaches with great difficulty. These buildings are very tall. A colleague and I went out with the intention of going to a nearby market, which was the Markale Market, to buy something, using money and also cigarettes, which also served as a currency. But halfway, and we were already close to Markale, we saw a large number of cars with sirens on, going very fast and passing us by. And from the open boots of those cars, you could see that they were full of bodies. There were limbs protruding. And the familiar was already -- the scene was already familiar to us that had already happened in many other incidents in Sarajevo. We knew already that this was work for us, and returned to base. We took the necessary equipment to analyse the crater, the azimuth, and everything else we needed, and we immediately proceeded to the site of the massacre, arriving, to estimate roughly, 10 or 15 minutes after we saw those cars full of wounded people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm now going to play a video. This is Video P1450. The total footage, Your Honours, that I propose to play is less than five minutes, but I'm going to play it in parts. And so the first is from 0 to 1 minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, could we stop the video. I'd like this to be played with sound, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe what you saw in those scenes, please.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It's one of the many cases of massacre that, in my deep conviction, were deliberate for their psychological effect. It was deliberate targeted terror and intimidation and pressure, probably on our authorities to make them more pliable in negotiations and, finally, to discourage the Bosnians, the whole population, the army, and our politicians, in terms of their struggle --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is it, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these are qualifications. It's not from his area of expertise. He's giving qualifications and going much broader, and he's putting me in a position that I have to deal with it in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you may cover that during your cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe, first of all, the removal of the bodies. Do you -- do you happen to know who the people are who are removing the bodies? Do you have any information whatsoever about that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Since these cases were very numerous in Sarajevo, those who removed the bodies and put them in cars, always trying to give first assistance, first aid, were always passersby. It's simply a reflex of the group, a humane impulse to help. Of course, these are all laymen. They don't know how to aid people. They think, naively, the best thing to do is to put them in a car and transport them to the nearest hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we now play the next 30 seconds, which is from 1 minute to 1 minute 30, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: First of all, could you say anything about the kinds of cars being used to transport the dead and the wounded?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, it's anything that passes by in that direction. Those are small cars like Yugo, Volkswagen, Golf. There was even a van. Anything that passes by and is able to take in and transport these bodies to the nearest hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And could you confirm the location that we're looking at in these video-clips, the general area?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I think directly in the middle of the picture we see the entrance to the market-place. The open-air area is also called "Markale." This is the northern entrance. There is another southern entrance on the other side. This is the place where the shell landed in the middle of this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask that we just go back to 1 minute and 28 seconds. Just freeze it there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: On the screen in front of you, you see the body of a person, and there appears to be little fluid underneath the body. Do you have any observations about that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: You see, first the height of the wound on this body absolutely corresponds to the angle at which the angle -- at which the shell fell. The shell fell in this part towards the south, I believe, at three and three and a half metres away, which is approximately the distance between me and you. And since the shell was inclined towards the south - relative to a vertical it would be 20 degrees - that means that the shrapnel that went from the shell towards this body were most concentrated in the area of the chest of this man, whereas we will see later that the shrapnel that went southwards hit people in lower extremities, hitting their legs and feet. You see how many concentrated shrapnel fell on this fence. Did you ask me about this stain below, if I remember correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My question was, specifically: There appears to be little fluid under the body. Do you have any comments about that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you see, from my lay knowledge - I'm not a medic - that the human body contains about five to six litres of blood, and if we know that the abdominal cavity and the lower extremities, which contain a lot of blood, are gravitationally vertical, and if we also know that the upper part of the chest, the head, and the arms are bent across this fence, and they contain, again, this blood which is no longer being pumped by the heart because the heart has stopped, I think -- here, I think there could be have been, in my lay estimate, around two litres of blood below this victim. In view of the viscosity of the blood, which, as it leaks onto the floor, does not spread into a stain, and if this wound looks open on the body, I believe it's an optical illusion and laymen would think that there should be more blood outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move now from 01:28 to 01:55, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This -- again, is this image consistent with death from a mortar round, just very briefly?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. A mortar shell of 120 millimetres is an artillery weapon by its calibre. It's part of the artillery range of weapons. It can produce a large number of shrapnel which, at high velocity, spread in a radial pattern in relation to the axis of the shell. And they are asymmetrical bodies, and as they fly after the explosion, they intensely rotate in all directions. In contact with the flesh, they rip apart the flesh, damaging it more than a bullet would of the same size. The direction of the motorcycle makes me conclude that at the point in time when the shrapnel hit him, that person was about to -- or had left the location where the impact was, and the distance he had covered was some five to ten metres from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we play now from 01:55 to 02:32, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We see, in this photograph, a person who appears to be in military uniform. Could you confirm, to the best of your knowledge, the extent to which Markale Market was frequented primarily by the civilian population, or partly by the military population, or what do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It was frequented by civilians by far. Perhaps, if a soldier had a break or some free time, they could be moving down that street or maybe they would have come to buy something. But in any case, they would be moving down that street. But in this place, the highest concentration of people who were there were civilians, people who were selling something or those who would come to buy something. It would mostly be food.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an invitation to speculate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, during the war, I was at this market at least 100 times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if you have an objection, raise it. It is not proper to interfere with the examination-in-chief by the OTP. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we now play from 02:32 to 03:25.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, we've dealt with this point. Actually, can we play on until 03:54. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, there's a -- there's a noticeable difference in the noise background in the last few seconds. Can you describe what we are looking at in this scene here? What are we looking at, exactly?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: From what I recall, these were French soldiers who had joined everyone and were doing their own investigation in order to establish the direction the projectile came from, the azimuth angle, and so on. I could hear them speaking French. They were on the scene briefly, from what I can remember. We can see the place of impact, and around it we don't see any bodies. In the previous clip that we saw, you could hear the voice of a man saying, Load everybody up. This was that spontaneous impulse that I was talking about of passersby who would simply join in this action of taking away all the dead and all the wounded urgently to the hospital. This is footage after a certain period of time, when things then proceeded to an analysis of the traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we play now from 03:54 to 04:40.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What do you understand the two soldiers are measuring in this scene?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: They're doing the same thing that we were doing independently of them. They are measuring the distance from the place of impact, the impact of the fuse, the precise point of contact of the projectile from the length of the wall of the market building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we play now from 04:40 to 05:22.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Actually, if we can just scroll back a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you -- back a few more seconds. Is that -- so forward one second. Thank you, Mr. Reid. Is that -- who is that in the background there?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That's me in the white shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we just play -- that was at 05:18. Could we play from now until 05:54.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in the last clip, we saw soldiers doing something. Are you in a position to say what it appeared they were doing?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The compass is used to measure the -- on the basis of the trace left by the shell. On contact, you can determine the bearing of fire; that is, the angle or the direction from which the shell came. That is the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I now ask for 65 ter 09900, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: While this is coming up: Could you describe what your personal role was in the investigation into the Markale 2 incident.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: My role, as well as the role of the team that had gathered in a large number at the point when the measurements were being done, was always the same; to collect, document, and properly process all relevant data that would indicate the place of impact, the angle of fall of the shell, the bearing, as well as the type of the weapon used or the type of the shell. Of course, all the relevant measurements are done that would improve and strengthen the calculations, make them more precise. For the final report, in order -- and all this is for the purpose of drafting a final report, where all our assertions would be properly supported and documented.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we go to photograph 4 of this 65 ter number, please. Could we zoom in to the photograph. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe what you see on the screen in front of you here.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: On the screen, you can see the trace left by any mortar shell on a hard surface. For purposes of analysis of the angle of fall and the bearing of fire, the best conditions are a hard surface. If you have a hard surface, that would provide the best evidence of the angle and the bearing of fire. You can see that the location has very heavy blood-stains. The traces are not very clear. And I also have reflection from the light above falling on my screen, so it's a little bit more difficult for me to see. I can see the distribution of shrapnel, indicating the possibility to make a calculation of the bearing. However, the left part from the center of the explosion of this collection of shrapnel is stained by blood which goes in a straight line, and that also conceals the exact pattern of the shrapnel on the ground. If the blood is washed away, this could be visible. The photograph, that is -- it's very -- the photograph -- the scope of the angle of the photograph is quite narrow. Perhaps if the -- compared to what you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll come back later to a version which you marked up in your earlier evidence. Could I now go to photograph number 10, please. Very briefly, could you describe whether this injury or this -- what you see in front of you, is this consistent with the impact of a 120-millimetre mortar projectile? If you need the screen to be moved, just let us know.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: We can see the part of the foot of a victim. In relation to the place of explosion, it is facing the south, in relation to the angle of the shell. And now I am reminding you of what I said in relation to the body of the victim that was thrown across the fence, which was on the north side of the fall of the shell, and the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is kindly asked to slow down and repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, Dr. Turkusic, the interpreters are having difficulty in interpreting your words. They say you are speaking a bit fast. Could you slow down a bit for them. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think I heard you, so could you repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it necessary to repeat something of what I have just said earlier so that the interpreters could correctly interpret it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the manner of wounding of this victim, whereby their foot was literally ripped off, corresponds completely to the angle of the fall of the shell, whereby this victim was located on the south side of the location of impact, because the shrapnel, in view of the angle of fall in this case, are spreading downwards, towards the road, towards the sidewalk. They fall lower in relation to the center of the explosion. The opposite case to this particular one is the wounding of that young man who was thrown and is bent over a fence, where the wound was sustained in the upper parts of the chest area. Both of these pieces of information about the place of wounding indicate the angle of the fall of the shell. This is not just one case of injury to lower extremities. There were a number of ripped feet, parts of the foot, heels, and all of this was on the sidewalk facing the market.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to tender the file of photographs for admission at this stage, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit P1926. And just to correct the record, the statement, 65 ter 22270, will be Exhibit P1925 and not P1924.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, did you -- were you involved in the determination of the minimum angle of the projectile at the moment of impact?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. In view of the geometry of the fall and the surrounding buildings, a serious examination of the direction and angle of the fall of the shell would imply the establishing of the smallest possible -- theoretically smallest possible angle of fall of the shell, below which angle it would be absolutely impossible for the shell to come in. This was one of our estimates. We measured the place of impact, its distance from the building, and the total height of the building from the flat roof of the building to the surface. We got the main parameters for the calculation of the incoming angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Karadzic, did you say something?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Excellency, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we call up 65 ter 09905, please. If we could show the English and the B/C/S side by side on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, for this portion, Mr. Turkusic, we're going to have to go back to a little bit of high school mathematics. First of all, could you just simply describe: What is the figure "11.45 metres" that we see in this diagram?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I said earlier that we measured -- two members of our team went to the roof of the market building, and they measured, from the roof, the height of the building. This is a cross-section of one part of that market building, only one part, where you can see the flat roof and where the height of the building is precisely stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The height of the building is 11.45 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you confirm that, as is marked in this diagram, that 4.8 metres is the distance from the edge of the building to the location of the impact and explosion of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That is correct. That is the distance that we measured accurately, and we could see on the video footage that the French artillery soldiers were also measuring that same distance. So this is now the second piece of data in this triangle used to establish the angle. This is the kathete of the triangle. And on the basis of those two parameters, one can precisely calculate the angle, which is 67.25 degrees, which, theoretically, is the smallest possible angle of the descent of the shell. With this drawing and this calculation, we are stating that that is the angle of the descent of the shell, and that is the smallest possible angle. Had the angle been smaller - and we checked that possibility as well - our team members who were on the roof did not see any traces, or markings, or damage at the edge of the building or on the roof of the building which would possibly indicate any ricochets. Had the shell dropped onto the roof, it would have stayed up there. It would have exploded and stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I just want to clarify part of your answer. You said there that you -- that this diagram shows the angle of impact. But to clarify, is this the angle of impact or is this the minimum possible angle of impact?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: You see, before we made the calculation of the angle of descent of the projectile, which is done in a different way, and we'll see that on the next picture, first of all, then we established the interval of possible angles. One end of the extreme would be this angle of 67 degrees, below which the shell did not descend. The other benchmark angle would be vertical, of 90 degrees, which theoretically and practically is actually impossible, because a shell would fall at an angle of 90 degrees only if it was fired vertically up in the air. So this possibility here is ruled out. In this particular case, we were ruling out this first extreme calculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'm just going to confirm a couple of things with you. If you would keep your answers short for this period. As a general matter, the tangent of an angle is the opposite over [Realtime transcript read in error "of"] the adjacent; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: By definition of elementary trigonometry, this level of mathematics, trigonometry, is something that any elementary school pupil would be able to calculate. The tangent of that angle is the length of the opposite kathete through the angled one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. My question should have read "the tangent of an angle is the opposite over the adjacent." I just want to confirm some figures. I want you to keep your answers very short for this period. The tangent of the angle was 2.385416; correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The tangent from alpha angle is 25384. The actual angle is in the inversion of function of the tangent. That is what would indicate the true value of the angle of 67 point something degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, you've anticipated my question, which is that alpha is the arc tangent of 2.38, et cetera; correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: 2.385, actually. Alpha is the arc tangent of 2.385, so the value of the alpha angle is the value of the arc tangent, which is the value of 2.3856, and that calculation would give you the exact number of the angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: To the right -- again, keep your answers fairly short for this period, Mr. Turkusic, please. We see a measurement based on a system whereby 360 degrees is 6.000 units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are many systems of dividing up a full circle into angles. One of the systems used by NATO is 6.400. From what I know in this division that was used in the former armija is the same one. The way in which we represented this angle in the 6.000 division is just an additional illustration. I think it is not that important in relation to the accuracy of the calculation. It's just a different way of expressing the values.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask that that be admitted, please, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1927, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in your previous answer, you said that they didn't see any damage at the top. Could you confirm that investigators went to the top of the building to inspect the building during the investigation?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct. They went up for two reasons; to check for any possible damage from the shell, which passed right along the edge of the building, and also to measure the height of the building, which is information that we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I call up now, please, 65 ter 10223. This is another diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Dr. Turkusic, now for this period, again I'm going to ask you a couple of questions. If you could keep your answers as short as possible for -- and then I'll indicate when you can expand a bit. This diagram shows a calculation of the likely angle of the projectile at the moment of impact; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, the distance X, which is marked at the bottom, how did you measure X?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That was measured as the distance between the place of impact, the contact of the fuse, the exact place where the shell came into contact with the ground, and the largest depressions from shrapnel which, like eyebrows, are engraved into the surface, but not in this same projection in which we are looking at the picture. That's the standard method used in all armies, written in all military books, about calculating the angle of descent, relying on the dimensions of the shell and the traces visible on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you explain, very briefly, first of all, what is the distance marked with the letter H?
