utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it not state in the first sentence here that: "On the 28th of August, at 11.30, the centre - Homicide Department - was informed that the center of the town had been shelled and that many --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we show the next page to the witness. Yes. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is: Who was clairvoyant enough to know an hour and a half before an event that shells would land? How do you account for this? How do you explain this?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't write the report. It could be a typographical error. 1130, 1330; it doesn't make a difference in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How can it be 1330 if the commission -- and you will see later on next to number 9, or below number 9, this was the commission which attended the scene on the 28th of August, 1995, at 12.15. The document does not leave room for lies.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, you use big words. There's no question of lying here. It says, below, information was collected on the spot; that on the 28th of August, 1995, at around 11.00, et cetera. I think it's a typographical error. I have nothing to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You investigated this. There was an impact at 11.00, at 11.30 you were informed, and at 12.15, you attended the scene; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No, that's not right. I wasn't informed by anyone. I attended the scene of my own initiative when I saw cars full of wounded and killed. A colleague of mine from KDZ and I, when we saw this, we went to the base to get our instruments. All these interventions were ad hoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your name next to number 5?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Asim Kanlic, a judge of the High Court of Sarajevo, appointed you to this commission; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: This is something I learned only at a later date. The commission was set up in a time of war. One cannot imagine, in such circumstances, having a protocol and all the various procedures. The commission was set up. I was at the spot -- at the scene at the time the commission was set up. I was unaware of it. At any rate, the commission came into its own later on with all the various analyses that were produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Later when?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, in the course of the following day. We worked hard throughout the night, making calculations. And I think that the main report -- you made mention of a court. Well, our report from the KDZ was -- had the date of the following day, which was when we produced our report. And for the rest, I would have to have a look and could only then give you my comments.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this an exhibit? It's a P exhibit, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it is already exhibited as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you proceeded to carry out an on-site investigation. Based on the minutes or the report from the on-site investigation, the investigating team was led by whom?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Can I see the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get -- can we see the last page of the document, the one bearing signatures.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who is mentioned here as the author of the text?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, attachment lists, and the report was made by Nedzad Zvizdic and Enes Cermagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Turkusic, did Lieutenant General Harry Konings attend these investigating procedures together with his investigating team?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: When my colleagues and I were at the scene, there were artillery members, and we saw them in the footage. There were others, but I didn't pay attention to them. I didn't have either the time or the interest to do so. We did our job properly, we took all the relevant data, we made our calculations -- or, rather, we would gather the data on the basis of which we would make calculations. You asked me about names, you asked me -- you gave me a name. I can't testify about that. I didn't introduce myself to anyone, nor did anyone introduce themselves to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You ascertained the direction of fire, did you not?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Not just I; my colleague and I. And the report was signed by our group leader. The important procedure we applied was as follows: Every member of the KDZ would independently write down the azimuth number based on their experience and knowledge. Next, we would compare our respective findings and establish that we have arrived at the same conclusion. So our azimuth is 170 degrees plus/minus 5 degrees, so the margin of error which -- this was the standard margin of error that we always had, and that was of plus/minus 5 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was it whom you established you arrived at the same conclusion?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, all of us from the KDZ. There was my colleague and I. We were later on joined by several other colleagues. Two of them went up on the rooftop to establish whether there had been a ricochet or a change of direction, and we measured the height of the roof. We talked about it in the first session. All of us were experienced in establishing the azimuth. And in order to minimise any errors, we each made our measurements independently. And by comparing our respective findings, we agreed that this was the direction of fire which we can -- could establish. Now, 15 years later, I can say that I am proud of the fact that the most competent teams of artillerymen confirmed our angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's not really the case, but let's leave it. Which is the table that you used; that the circle was 6.000 or 6.400?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: 6.000. We would have the division of a circle into 6.000. This is a table that is less frequently used. Mathematically and technically, it makes no difference if we use a circle for the establishment of the azimuth as that of 6.000 or 6.400. It's the same thing as if you referred to five oranges in a different system of weights, but it's always the same number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. But did you use 6.000 or 6.400?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: 6.000. The conversion of degrees we used was that of 6.000, which, in technical terms, means nothing; the angle is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The azimuth you determined was one which could have been 165 degrees. Isn't that almost straightforward south?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, it's 5 degrees -- it's full south short of 5 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the azimuth determined or established by the French investigators?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I reviewed all these reports, but as I sit here now, I can't remember which were the ones they established or others. It's a matter in the public domain, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just a brief interpretation correction. Where it says "165 degrees," I believe the original might have been "175 degrees."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That should be clear. Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, that's correct, 170 plus/minus 5. So it could be 175, which is almost straightforward south.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So are you familiar with the fact that the French established the azimuth at 2.850, which is, in actual fact, 160 degrees?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, if that's a document that exists and that's in the possession of the Court, that's all very well, but I would never sign a document with such a calculation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 65 ter 15060. 65 ter 15060, page 29.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P1447, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see a 65-degree angle here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you see "2.850"?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I would have to have a calculator now to see, and I would have to know which division was the one that they use, 6.000 or 6.400, which isn't something I can tell from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Didn't the French in the NATO --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They wouldn't use --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Be slower, please. They couldn't hear from your question: "Didn't the French in the NATO ..." And then they stopped.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked if the French were in NATO, and then the witness said, Yes. So then I said that I suppose that the French use not the Russian table but a NATO table, and the witness confirmed it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I know, the English are a member of NATO as well, but they confirmed our calculations and the angle of 175 degrees. So they added the 5 degrees and stuck by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But which of the tables were used; 6.000 or 6.400?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What I wanted you to do is to repeat your question, instead of wrapping up on your part. What was your question? It's not clear to us what the question was and what the answer was. In any event, it's time to take a break now. We'll have a break for half an hour. But before that, Mr. Tieger, I forgot to ask you this morning regarding the witness schedule for next week. I asked you to get back to us by today, morning. Can I hear the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Turkusic will be the last witness, in view of the Court's order. No other witnesses present or in transit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you will come back to us by Wednesday, whether there are any witnesses who are locked in specific dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll resume at 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue. For your scheduling purpose, we will have a short break, 10 minutes or 15 minutes, at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was advised that -- from the Court Deputy that the interpreters and the court reporters have kindly agreed to go on until 5.00 today. Is it agreeable to the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, it's agreeable to us. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you again. Yes, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the participants and for the learned Mr. Gaynor, in the case against General Milosevic, on the 19th of February, 2007, on page 2418 -- 7-2418, this witness said he arrived at Markale after about 10 minutes -- about 10 minutes after the incident, that is. And then on page 2419, he said he was very close, that the bomb squad was very close to the bank, the central bank that is nearby. And then on page 2549, he said that at the time of the explosion, he was en route to the market to buy cigarettes, and they went back to get their equipment straight away, and in about seven or eight minutes, they were on the scene of the incident. So during the explosion, he was in the street, and he came with his equipment at about -- in about 10 minutes, at 1305 hours. That is what his statement said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, did the UN monitors inform you that they did not see any kind of firing coming from the Serbian side or across the line of separation?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I know, from the monitors - some of them were not in Colina Kapa - that there was no firing registered from the northern site of Trebevic, where our positions were, definitely. Since no firing was heard from that side of Trebevic, that is definitely proof that the firing came from the top or the other side of Trebevic that was then under the control of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that case, that shell would have to fly over them; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Depending on the charge, 0 plus X, going all the way to 6, it has different trajectories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, please don't hold this against me. Let's not go into theory. This particular shell, would it have to be registered by a radar, and would it have to be observed by the monitors, in view of the charge? Not theoretically; this particular one.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Monitors cannot see a shell. They can only hear the firing and the fall. Their report says that the firing, that was an exceptionally strong explosion, had not been noticed by these monitors, which absolutely rules out the possibility, theoretical, practical and any other, that it had been fired from our positions, because then they would have heard it. Radar would be another way of doing this. What was your question in relation to the radar?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The radar did not register any kind of firing from the Serb side; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: You see, the closest airport to us is the Amsterdam Airport, and the radar there is not going to register any aircraft flying from Munich to America, because that's the way it's adjusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about Cymbeline radars that register shells, and UNPROFOR had them.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That radar scans a particular area. If a shell happens to be flying above that area, the radar sees several points, and its software analyses its trajectory, analyses its ballistic trajectory, and where it falls. The radar observes, under quotation marks, this area, and then we will see this shell. But if it is not adjusted, it will not. So if the shell comes above or below the radar, as it were, it cannot register it, as I explained in the case of the aeroplane a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if it flies below the beam, it will not register it. But if it goes above the beam?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said the minimum angle of descent; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the minimal theoretically possible angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If it were less than that, the shell would have to go through the building?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't go through the building. It would stay on the roof, due to explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the maximum angle for a 120-millimetre shell is what?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Maximum? Well, a crew can fire a shell vertically at 90 degrees, so there is no limit. So that's the maximum angle, 90 per cent [as interpreted]. It's a paradox, but it's true. And the minimal possible angle is the one that we had determined.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You determined the minimal one. Did you establish what the actual real angle was of this shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Precisely. If you followed the first session today, we conducted two measurements and two calculations with parameters that are absolutely independent. The first one meant setting the minimal possible angle under which we rule out the smaller one. That was the objective of the first measurement. The second measurement that we carried out, and on the basis of which we did our calculation, was the measurement that, according to all books that relate to the relevant mortar and the projectiles, is based on mathematical conclusions, and our calculation had to do with the most probable angle of impact of this shell. It's about 3 degrees bigger than the possible one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 10223. That's the 65 ter number I'd like in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you help us -- can you explain to us how you calculated this real, actual angle? You said that Point C is the point of the explosion and that H is from the vast array of literature that you had; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Point C is crucial for these relations here, right, for these numerical relations and for determining the real angle; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Since the explosive wave hydrodynamically spreads through this mass, the center of explosion is always taken as the center of the mass involved, because the entire mass of the explosive explodes at a particular moment, regardless of whether it's closer to the tail or closer to the fuse. And the center of explosion is where the explosion is strongest, and it corresponds to the center of the mass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The center of the explosion corresponds to the center of the mass?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, in the theory of hydrodynamic waves in ultra-rapid reactions. It is well known that explosives do not burn like a fuse in real time but by way of hydrodynamic waves, and at the same time it is activated in its entire volume. And the strongest explosion is concentrated in the center of the mass of the explosive involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the French team established the center of the mass, not the center of explosion, because they do not know of that concept? They said the center of the explosion, and this H is much longer than in your case. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't, but that doesn't impress me at all. I don't have to honour a document that I've never seen or analysed. Please show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that their findings are different from yours?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know until I see it, so show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. When we can, we will show that to you. And do you know that others from the United Nations had different views on this?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I am not exactly well-versed in the analyses of others with regard to the angle of descent. But anything that you would like to deal with, could I please have it on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we're going to have your sketch, 65 ter 14404, and then page 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that: Without knowing the angle of descent, it is not possible to set the range or to see the place from where it was fired; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the depth of the crater in the case of this shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember right now, but we will easily find it in the KDZ report. The depth of the crater, well, one of them is the one that corresponds to the point of impact. It is a very specific radial. And the other one is a projection of the radial spreading from the axis of the shell, and depending on the angle involved, it creates a different picture on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What we mean by that is what the fuse does, the bottom, what this shell does to the ground once it falls. Do you remember that in the case of Markale 1, there was a 120-millimetre mortar shell and that its tail-fin got stuck 9 centimetres into soil that was rather hard?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall that, but what you're saying is not correct. The soil that the tail-fin got stuck in was a lot softer. It is tarmac, like in the case of Markale 2, but it is a pedestrian area, it's a market. And, therefore, it is much less firm than where 20-ton trucks move. So when the surface is softer, because of the acceleration on impact and because of the vacuum during the explosion, the fuse falls with the same velocity. At the moment of explosion, the fuse moves even faster and it literally sticks into the ground if the surface can take it. In the case of Markale, it was different, although the surface looked the same; it was tarmac in both cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to wait for the interpretation. Can you mark on this photograph the place where the fuse was found? Sorry, stabiliser, tail-fin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Should we not turn around this sketch?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Clockwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's fine, but let's zoom in a bit further, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it. There's no need for it. The place where the fuse fell is not the one that we established. I think it was done by the CSB Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, not the fuse; sorry.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Tail-fin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the place of impact? I don't think we've got the north indicating in the right direction. Do we have north marked on here?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it should be right up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The market is on the south, and the other end is north, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the place of impact?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't make this sketch, or analyse it, but if -- in relation to this motorist, if what we see to the left is west, what we see up there is south, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it should be flipped by 180 degrees?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't mind it as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. It will be rotated. Can you mark the place of impact and the place where the tail-fin was found?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I can't give any information about the tail-fin, because it was the CSB that found it, photographed it, and marked it with a number. The position of the tail-fin was mentioned in some of the reports by foreign military forces. My team and I, in other words, did not find the tail-fin or measure the distance from where the tail-fin was to the place of impact. Although the sketch is quite unclear, if the square stands for the town market, and if this is the tarmac where we see numbers 1 through 5, though upside down, what we see to the left is the motorcycle leaving, then the place of impact of the shell should be [marks] -- oh, I happened to touch the screen with the pen. I didn't intend to place this dot. So this is probably this position 1 [marks], though it's very difficult for me to interpret this sketch because this is the first time that I'm looking at a representation of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I were to assist you by referring to a key, would you recall that where we have number 9, although it's upside down so it's 6, would you agree that this is 30 metres away from impact?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you. I can't even testify about where the tail-fin was found. Let me repeat that the CSB found the tail-fin, photographed it, marked it with a number, labelled it with a number, and it's referred to in the reports by foreign teams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There should be a legend about these indications, and an interpretation as well. Why do we have to ask the witness to mark the place where something has been found?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the legend, or the key, is on the previous page. So could we have a split screen with both?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is all a waste of time. Just put your question. All the materials are before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know that the minimum range of a 120-millimetre shell, with a primary charge is 300 metres and with a secondary charge is 400 metres, and that it cannot reach beyond that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, the parameters you mentioned are roughly those, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that, according to the legend, the tail-fin is under number 12, though it's upside down, and that it's 30 metres from the place of impact, would that tell you anything about the range or the speed at which the shell hit the ground?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No. When hitting ground that it cannot penetrate, the tail-fin elastically deforms itself. If you ever watched billiards, you would know what it means when you have two balls hitting each other. So when it cannot penetrate the ground, the tail-fin would basically ricochet off the ground and then end up in whatever is close by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, could you tell us the English page for this legend?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Certainly. I'll look for that immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's 31 in Serbian; perhaps in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If a shell runs at a very high speed, then the explosion will certainly not affect the tail-fin, but if the shell flies at a very low speed, then the explosion would basically push the tail-fin away?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No. This makes no sense.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 25 in English, and I want a split screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think we have to keep that marking. We can go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then we don't need the legend either?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need it. I think it's from page 24 to 25. Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, that sounds about right. I'm trying to count through the pages. That's right, but on 65 ter 14404. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There, 1 through 9, but it continues on to the next page, because there should be 12 in all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can have it, so you can continue without having to show that page. Now we can see it on our own.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have P1450. Will you broadcast it? So we'll broadcast the portion we're interested in. Channel 2 should be changed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what you observed. The time is 3 minutes 50. Tell us, please, at which point does a shell fragment?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Because of a very high fragmentation rate, it is called a "contact-action fuse." It happens so fast that you cannot possibly split the time to analyse it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So at the point when fragmentation is complete, as many fragments as you had in a split second, that's how many fragments you will find; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, how big must a fragment that can split the chest this way be?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, a fragment of some seven, eight centimetres tore a part of a man's feet, so if we have -- a part of a man's foot. So if we have the entire chest broken and we have shells arriving not radially but spinning, then they will have the effect of destroying the entire chest. And, in fact, the height at which we see it tallies with the trajectory, and I'm referring to my answer where I had to draw a red line to indicate what the lines meant. Those were the lines of the densest fragmentation of shrapnel which spreads out in space perpendicularly to the axis of the shell. And if we look at the dimensions of the street, the distance was three and a half, four metres, perhaps, so that's less of a distance than there is between the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Turkusic, will you agree with me that, in addition to five litres of blood, a man would have several litres of lymph and some 40 litres of tissue liquid?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, that's ridiculous, because you can't possibly extract the liquid that is present throughout the tissue of a human being. So that particular liquid cannot be counted into the picture; only the blood, which is under pressure up until the point the heart ceases to beat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that arteries had to have been ruptured here and there had to be an arterial haemorrhage as well?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, for a brief period of time, for as long as the pressure in the arteries exist. However, in this case, it's very difficult for me to say anything. The heart certainly didn't beat for as long as to pump up all the arterial blood that we can see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Our case, Mr. Turkusic, is that the entire story around Markale 1 and Markale 2 has been invented, and has been constructed in order to provoke NATO bombing, which was true, and that all the bodies, these corpses, were actually brought here from elsewhere, and they were, in the process, treated with complete and utter disrespect, they were packed into cars and lorries, and this is something that, in our culture, one does not do with dead bodies and dead people. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I tell you that you should not have referred to the term "culture." And let me just say that the thesis that you present is identical to the thesis that the English, in World War II, with rockets F1 and F2, hit London in order to attach or attribute this and lay the blame at the Germans.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's see 1D -- let's look at the following footage, the next frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the French photographing a tail-fin of a 120-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't see why you think these are the French. What I can see from the man's sleeve is that they are members of the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that it was first the French UNPROFOR members who reached the site and conducted their investigation?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: This isn't something I can confirm. At that point in time, it wasn't the most important thing for us to see, who arrived at the scene first, second, or third. Under the circumstances, anything of the sort was impossible to detect and note.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that UNPROFOR members are photographing and making note of a tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to your information, who was it who reached the scene first?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Since I got there with my colleague, as I said, when the wounded and dead had already been taken away, I only found body parts; feet, hands, bits of brain, and other body parts at the scene. So roughly about that time, those who were among the first reached the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So some 10 minutes after the explosion, you got there, and 10 minutes later, therefore, 10 minutes after the explosion, the place had been evacuated and the bodies had been taken away; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I repeat, I got at the scene some 10 minutes after I saw vehicles driving away the dead and the wounded. When I saw the vehicles, I went back to the office to get my equipment, and returned to the scene, which must have taken an additional 10 minutes. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you arrived there 20 minutes after you had seen corpses being driven away, and an unknown number of minutes after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No. According to my rough estimate, which, given the circumstances, may be mistaken, after I saw cars full of bodies driving along the street, I realised that there was a massacre, which wasn't something that was unusual at the time in Sarajevo, I got back -- I went back to my office. You have to factor in the time that I took to reach my office and return to the scene. Now, we were able to see at the beginning of this footage the speed at which the events took place, where individuals were, as soon as possible, put into vehicles and driven away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you got there, dead bodies and the wounded were already evacuated. Did these French arrive there before you?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot possibly confirm or deny what you're saying. How would I know when the French got there, if those were the French, the ones we look at here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They are the UNPROFOR members. Were the members of the CSB the ones who first reached the scene or were those the French?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I told you already that we did not observe or take care to see who got there first. It would have been absurd of us to even attempt such a thing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D2732. Sorry, we will get to the tail-fin with the help of the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, we have to establish who got there first. That's very important. Who secured the scene? Who got there first, who got there second, et cetera? Did the police get there before UNPROFOR? Is it at all possible for you to give us an answer or does it not matter, as you say? Well, we think it matters because -- who left the tail-fin behind, this tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I think that several members of the CSB and UNPROFOR members - let me refer to them in this way - materialised there before my colleague and I and the rest of my team got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At any rate, the local police was there before UNPROFOR; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I can only assume. I cannot confirm. It may have happened the other way around. Neither you nor I have evidence to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will be asking for evidence to that effect. Is this the tail-fin in question?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, to the best of my recollection, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What sort of force would effect such a change on these wings?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: A smaller passenger vehicle and, of course, a larger vehicle. Any vehicle larger than a small vehicle, because the tail-fin is made of a very thin and soft tin. They are intended to direct the shell rather than be resilient to any impact, so basically one can bend them with the strength of a foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is what you're trying to say that shortly after the explosion, a lorry appeared and destroyed the tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Why are you imputing this to me? This isn't something that I said. After the explosion, the vehicles that arrived there certainly paid no attention to any tail-fins of any sort, and it is possible that a couple of them drove over it. I didn't say "a lorry." I said that even a small vehicle would do this. It would not smash it, but it could deform it in this way, because, let me repeat, the wings are very fragile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see the part of the tail-fin called the cap?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the cap did not fall off; it's still there?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It never falls off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what we are talking about: We are talking about the cap. Is it there?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: If that's the one that you can find on any bullet, coming from a gun, or a rifle, or whatever, it's there. It's possible that it's inside, because when it is activated, it's even pushed inside by the needle. But most probably, yes, viewed from this angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see erosion on the body of the tail-fin, around these holes?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Which holes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the body of the tail-fin, closer to the body itself. Do you see the erosion? Has it eroded?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that you're not very familiar with this term, "erosion." You don't really know what it is. When there is such a strong explosion, the body of the tail-fin, which is made of relatively soft material, can be deformed in this way. It is not surprising at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not disputing it. I'm just asking whether you claim or confirm that this body had eroded.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No, I am denying what you're saying, that that's erosion that is reminiscent of corrosion and all of that is supposed to mean that it had been stuck somewhere for a long time. This is precisely what it looks like after an explosion like this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll go back to that. Let us now see part of the film and the photograph from the film that shows -- actually, it's 27:32.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is the view from the east, in relation to the entrance, or, rather, is this the view from Bascarsija?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the center of the explosion here in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where it is?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: If this, what one can discern on the left, is the entrance, then the center of the explosion is a bit lower than that. It is on the sidewalk, in that case. However, with so many wounded and dead that are concealing the center of the explosion, it is practically invisible. One can only indirectly speculate about this, if we want to have exact references.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I seem to have to wait a little. Do you see this whitish mass on the ground and on the sidewalk? What is that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Now that it's been zoomed in, it's still hard to say, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could it be glass?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't rule that out, because when there is such a blast, such an explosion, such a detonation, most of the glass that is in that area simply shatters. However, I'm not claiming that it is glass, but it's quite possible that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the skirt of this woman, do you see traces of shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, on her right leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And around them and further in depth, where the shell is, we see this whitish mass or, rather, glass; right? Or, rather, no, whitish mass, some whitish mass, right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, around these people, and further on where the shell fell. Do you see that there, this whitish/bluish mass?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot call it a bluish/whitish mass, because I simply don't know what it is. A photograph with this kind of a zoom and under such circumstances and this blur, I cannot discern anything, I cannot say exactly what things are. This is a lighter field. If we're talking about glass, it could also be a litre of spilled milk that would create this kind of a white field, but that is a level of speculation that I don't want to go into.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see a man down there whose hand is indicating the car there?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Is there a yellow car behind him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, the car that's on the road.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't see that. I don't understand what you are saying. You have an indicator in your hand, so perhaps you can show me what you're referring to. I see this arrow, or cursor, so why don't you show me what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that? Is this a man whose hand is pointing towards the car?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It may be put that way, but not with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a look at the next one, the next clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see that that man was alive?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Which man?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The one whose hand was pointing to the car.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. As the film continued, we saw that that which we may recognise as a hand was going down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These two men who we saw now in the previous image are on the street, itself; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Which two men? The one with his hand down is one, and who's the other one?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1 minute 34, let's move on. From 32 to 36, that's the seconds that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that these two men are alive at the very point of impact of the shell?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We saw the first man. Who is the second man you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to play it, and then you're going to see that there is two men there and that they are both alive.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move on? 1.34.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I respond to what you asked me a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the height of the shell and the density of shrapnel, and in view of the axis of the shell, people who are wounded in the lower limbs stand a far greater chance to survive after the explosion than those who are a bit further away from the shell and who are hit in the upper part of their bodies. As you know full well, that's where the most vital bodily parts are. So your suggestion that this man close to the point of impact is still alive may mean that he had lost both legs. Sarajevo is full of people like that now, and they were very close to the explosion, and that's why they lost their legs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now go from 1.34 to 1.37 to show that no one's touching that man. He is there as if nothing were happening. He doesn't seem to be attracting anybody's attention, and he is precisely in the place where the shell had impacted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 1.34 to 1.37.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the place where the shell impacted?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot discern the point of impact when I have this kind of resolution. I would have to see the exact imprint that the shell created when it exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, in view of the fact that the accused is claiming that this was a staged incident, could I request that he play the video with volume to assist Your Honours in determining whether or not this incident was a staged incident? With the volume on, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough. But we are still waiting for the scene referring to the two alive men. Are you going to withdraw that question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I'm not going to withdraw that question. I just -- actually, let me just show you what this looks like, what the traces look like here. Please, can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At this time, can we play it with sound.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go back to that other part, the one that we had announced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's Mr. Marko Sladojevic that's playing the video. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Frame for frame [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] Frame by frame, please. Let us just see the man with the bag. If you had planned a break, could we consult during the break about these seconds?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll break for about 15 minutes, and we'll resume at 10 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As you can notice, we are sitting pursuant to 15 bis for the remainder of today. Judge Morrison is away due to urgent business. I would like to express the Chamber's appreciation to the interpreters and court reporters for their agreement to work for extended hours. We deeply understand how difficult it is to work for such a long time, given the concentration they need in order to perform their function. We'll sit until 5.00 today. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence joins your expression of gratitude, all the more so because we speak so fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, do you agree that on this picture, we see two men whose heads are facing the center of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No. I do not recognise what you claim, nor the opposite, by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When we play it, we'll see. Do you agree that this man's trousers are torn?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that either. The time of the massacre is the 28th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it's visible on the picture.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: You mean the one with white trousers?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, the one close up.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, and we can see traces of shrapnel on his lower limbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The one closer to us, does he have trousers on?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I can't see that, because the white thing we see could be shorts. It was August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The man in front, does he have legs?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I can't say that either, because if the one closer to us is lying on the other man, then he's lying on his legs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next clip. Please look closely at the man who is just raising his head where the cursor points. Can we now play it to see how far he raises his head, and his shoulders as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look closely at this photograph. Do you see this pattern of shrapnel around this man and on his bag?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. What pattern?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see around him a pattern, a drawing made by the shrapnel, and on his back? Was this man lying when the explosion happened? Does it fit into the picture?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Not at all. This bag lying on the ground, and the pattern of shrapnel, would not be at all looking like this if the bag had been lying on the ground when the explosion happened, because then the shrapnel would have hit from the side. And precisely the shrapnel on the bag tells us that during the explosion, this woman or man was standing vertically. You can see that the bag was vertical, upright.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain the pattern of shrapnel around him, because the shrapnel fell vertically, as you say, and there is the same pattern on his bag?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: What I see on the back of this person, on the jacket and what I see on the bag is consistent with the vertical position of the body at the time of the explosion of the shell, because this even disposition of shrapnel holes in the bag would have been impossible if the bag was lying at the moment of explosion. That bag must have been hanging alongside the body of the victim, as if he or she was standing vertically, upright.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For me, Mr. Turkusic, this picture -- this pattern on the bag is consistent with the pattern on the asphalt. The man was lying at the moment of the explosion. It's, again, an old corpse, just set there to frame this explosion, to set it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2728.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear your last question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It was the number, Your Honour. The number was repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you just made a statement, and you didn't have to, but you didn't respond to Mr. Gaynor's intervention that your case is that this scene was staged. Can I ask you whether it is your case that this scene was staged?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I affirm that those few incidents, with massive casualties, were altogether -- they were not more than 100 victims here in the center of the city, at Markale, were staged by the BH Army with the view to involving NATO and the international community into the war. Most of the bodies were brought from the front-line, bodies already dead. You can see that from the man whose half thoracic cavity is missing. They are dumping bodies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you should put that question to the witness. Witness, earlier on the accused said: "What I see on the back of this man's jacket and on the bag is consistent with the time of the shell, because this --" No. "... jacket and on the bag is consistent with the time of the shell -- as the pattern on the asphalt, because this even disposition of shrapnel holes in the bag would have been impossible if the bag was lying at the moment of explosion. That bag must have been hanging alongside the victim, as if --" Sorry, is that the question or answer? Yes: "That bag must have been hanging alongside the victim as if he or she had been --" That's your answer. But after that, the accused said: "For me, Mr. Turkusic, this picture -- this pattern on the bag, is consistent with the pattern on the asphalt. The man was lying. It's just a corpse set there to frame this explosion, to set it." Do you have any comment to that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just, for the record, add -- it is not on the record. I said the explosion happened here, but most of the bodies were laid there before, and the way they treat these bodies shows that those were old corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What do you say to that, Mr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: In forensic medicine, these are elementary things. How old a corpse is can be determined up to an hour or two, or even a few days, but it can be determined exactly. After the bodies were taken to Kosevo Hospital, large numbers of journalists, UNPROFOR members, and other people interested in photographing and examining these bodies, and anybody and everybody was able to see from the appearance of those corpses how old they were, whether it was 10 or 15 days or half an hour. Those are elementary things in forensic medicine. I am not the proper witness for this. You would need an expert in forensic medicine. But I claim that what I said are elementary things that refute this kind of speculation or view of yours, which is the only thing that could possibly be more monstrous than this scene, itself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 1D2730.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting: Let me tell you, Mr. Turkusic, we will prove here that none of those people made even an external examination of the body. Do you know of any external examination of the bodies, at least, that were submitted to you, let alone a post-mortem report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to say if Mr. Karadzic wishes to put his case to the witness, he's welcome to do that, but it sounded like he was either arguing with the witness or making submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I agree. Yes, what is your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is: Mr. Turkusic said that a large crowd of people gathered around the bodies to see them. My question is: Did their investigation team receive at least an external description of the bodies, let alone a post-mortem? We saw that some foreigners came and saw some bodies in a hole, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you receive an external description of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That question is properly addressed to another witness. I did not go to the place where the bodies were collected or the wounded were placed, nor did I receive any report about that later, because that was not my job or my responsibility. But I'm sure that there are detailed reports about the condition of those bodies, and you can distinguish between two hours from death and two days from death very easily and very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that these young men from your army who transported these bodies called them frozen and kept them in refrigerators, in freezers?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I hear that for the first time. You can show me a document, if you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Later. Do you agree that on this post, on this lamppost, the traces of fragments are opposite to the place of explosion?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It's not a rare occurrence that these and such lampposts are pierced by shrapnel. You can find them in Sarajevo still today, because the enormous kinetic energy can pierce the post from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wouldn't this hole look different? Wouldn't the exit hole look different? These are entry holes.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I do not associate them with this explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, did any other explosion happen here?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 1D2725.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Karadzic is suggesting that he may have documents showing that young men from the ABiH transported these bodies, called them frozen, and kept them in refrigerators, in freezers. I'd invite him to tender his documents to the Court as soon as he possibly can so that we can show them to witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Can you give us a reference or can you show us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our military service filmed that or recorded it, so we would need to reach the military service, and I'm now separated from all these structures. But those who follow this broadcast will know what I want and will send it to us. But I know at that time, we had access to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you said "these young men from your army." Who did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The army of Mr. Turkusic, those who staged this scene. They kept those bodies for several days, and on radio they were heard talking about ice blocks. And their commander warned them to stop talking and to keep silent. Our service intercepted it, and I'm about to receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's -- that's precisely the sort of conversation you can fabricate with radio equipment. You can establish a communication line on the radio, you can have people talking on one side, and record them on the other. Your Honours, every time I asked Mr. Karadzic to show me a document when he made a claim, he said, I will. And now that the time of my testimony is running out, there are four or five documents he was about to show me, and I think that he is not going to show me any of the documents he owes me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't owe you anything, except this recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you that in the Milosevic case, you said that at the time of the explosion, you said you were on your way to the market, and you arrived there within 10 minutes. I gave you the pages of that transcript.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: You didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I told the OTP what page it was. Let them give it to you. Do you see this photograph, Mr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the man sitting next to the woman in the purple dress?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Is this -- do you mean somebody behind her?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right next to her, behind her.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I can see something that could be a person's back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see the man who's lying in the street behind the man in the black suit?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is his head facing the direction from which the projectile came?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I do not see clearly where the head is facing, the head of the person lying behind the man in the black suit. You cannot see that clearly from that picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But can you confirm that the place where the shell landed is just behind the man in the black suit?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot see the entrance to the market on this picture. From this angle, you can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you now see those two men that I said had their heads facing towards the place of the explosion here in the right corner?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are their heads facing the place of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot see the place of the explosion here. It could have been both to the left or to the right, because you cannot see the trace of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it in the opposite direction of the direction where the heads on the pavement are facing?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Some were propelled by the blast in one direction, and some were wounded, were left standing for a second or two, and then fell to the ground in a direction that is determined by nothing except by the free falling of a dead body.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Together with the previous picture showing the lamppost?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There are three photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have been shown two photos. They will be admitted. I see no problem. That's a part of that video-clip, the still images from that video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, they appear to be still images from that video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits D874 to 876 respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So three; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Turkusic, the crater and the entire place, what were they cleaned with and whitewashed with before the arrival of UNPROFOR so that there is not a single trace of blood?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, we saw an image where we have an imprint of the shrapnel, and we have the image where the wing was recovered. When we were discussing azimuth, I drew your attention to that. Chalk is used to mark the depression or the impression of the shell, and in this way the crater, itself, is made more visible for the purposes of the analysis and photography.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will see the crater now when the French arrive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very briefly, an interpretation correction. I think the word "wing" should probably mean "stabiliser."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the crater is quite clean? What has it been cleaned with?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there a possibility that only after the departure of the French, blood was spilled over?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: This is a speculation that cannot be addressed to me. I cannot either confirm it or deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Turkusic. Let's move on to a different incident. Did you investigate the incident at Safeta Zajke Street?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It does sound familiar. Can we -- can I have the document shown on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It happened on the 24th of May, 1995. It was formerly Zrinska Street, now Safeta Zajke Street. Can we have 65 ter 09786, page 3. 65 ter 09786, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall this conclusion, this finding? Have a look, and tell us what it was that you did in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I have to see the first page in order to give you a complete answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 1 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was written in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That does not exist. Vuk Karadzic was the one who created the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: He certainly did not create the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see here "the 24th of May," and you were delivered something to work on it? Let's look at your -- what you said about it in the statement.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, we have the specification of the material that was delivered to us. Five steel deformed pipes; two iron deformed sheets of tin; five meshy rings, et cetera. So -- five lattice rings. So I've only looked at a couple. We can all see what the document contains. Can we now have page 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your amalgamated statement, this can be found at item 5. Please have a look at that as well. What was it that you did in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: We were asked to carry out a forensic examination to establish the calibre and type of the projectile, but I can't see the relevant part. This is just the introductory part where we are stated -- we are told what we are supposed to do with the material that was given to us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the forensic examination has established as follows; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a device which was most probably made of a contact fuse aerial bomb and five rockets of the Grad type, so this is a description relating to the examination of a modified air-bomb which was launched on Sarajevo on several occasions within a short span of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your boss signed it, and you wrote it; right? Look at number 5 in your statement.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: What is number 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Incident number 5, or job number 5. That's page 8 of your report.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I can't find it here. Is it the one with my initials, that page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, you must have it in your hands. Right? Very well. What is written here, and I'm translating from English: "I investigated the attack with a modified air-bomb which exploded on the 24th of May, 1995, in Safeta Zajke Street number 3, Sarajevo. We produced a report about this incident. I confirm the facts and conclusions that are stated in the report are true." Is this your position?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The way you present it here, I don't accept it, because you're translating from English a document which I don't have before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You stated this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry. To clarify, the witness appears to get lost. Mr. Karadzic is quoting from your amalgamated statement, Mr. Turkusic. And subject to the Court's direction, if you want to see a copy of that, we can give that to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to see your statement, Mr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because it will most certainly be directly related to the question that will be put to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It would be helpful if you could hand over the photocopy, if you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. What's the para number?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It was on page 5. I'd have to find my other --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 8, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you had a look at it?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Can you direct me to the passage that you've just read out in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 5, and paragraph 1 was what I read. There's a footnote 15 there, which is 65 ter 09786, and footnote 16 is your statement which you gave to this Tribunal on the 1st of December, 1996. So do you agree that this is the case?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D02 -- 2199. I skipped some things in order for us to finish sooner. I -- or, rather, to cut the time short, we will not be changing it. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark here the crossroads of Esad Midzic and Safeta Zajke Streets? Is that where the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: You're asking me something that happened 15 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the report, or look at your statement.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Very well. Safeta Zajke. You can help me by indicating the street as it is on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where what was formerly Zrinska Street was?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: North of the railway line, is that Zrinska Street, and then you have Esad Midzic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: You mean above the tobacco factory?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's right. Do you see the wire factory there?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, north of the wire factory, Esad Midzic Street?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that where the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Esad Midzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Safeta Zajke, where it intersects with Esad Midzic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: It might well be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You got that order. Where is that document we looked at earlier? What did you precisely receive? 1D2634. Can we have 1D2634 on the left-hand side and keep the map on the right-hand side. Can we rotate by 90 degrees -- no, 180. The position is not right. Just a moment. Do you agree that Safeta Zajke runs east-west or west-east and that Esad Midzic runs to the north? Right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this sketch help you remember the incident which you were charged with to investigate?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I don't recall this sketch at all, and I don't know who did it. I don't think I did. And as for the specification we looked at quickly, what we were asked to do had nothing to do with this sketch. Rather, through the examination of several pieces, we were to establish what happened, i.e., what it was that exploded. We were also supposed to describe the origin of the material we were provided with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You established that what was most probably the case -- or, rather, did you make an assertion with certainty or probability?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Where did you read that we said that it was most probably this and that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 9786 was the document, page 3. So you can't mark anything on the map?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, there's no need for that. The CSB tasked us with analysing the material they provided us with.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have that 65 ter document, please. We need page 2 -- page 3. Page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is the document signed by your boss, which you drafted. You will remember that you worked on it?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is a device most probably made up of -- right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the basis on which you concluded that it was a contact fuse air-bomb?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the fact that many such bombs were launched on Sarajevo, by the fact that they had rocket engines, there are not many contact fuse bombs -- or, rather, sorry, contact fuse air-bombs. There are not many types of those, in view of their destructive power, and the fragments that were left behind were thick pieces, which show that the bomb had a very thick steel wall. And in view of the elements that kept the parts of the bomb, that kept it together -- parts of the rocket, we made this conclusion, as we said, "most probably."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was the destructive power of the bomb?
