utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Enormous. In view of the total mass of an air-bomb, roughly half of it is, from what I remember, the explosive mass. So you could actually calculate that half of the weight of the bomb is due to TNT.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what did you conclude that it had five 122-millimetre Grad-type rockets?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of the parts we were provided with, because normally you have the power unit of the rocket, which is at its end, and the explosion propels the unit, and it can always be found somewhere in the perimeter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The parts of the engine that were recovered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I intervene at this moment. For the planning purpose, Mr. Karadzic, you have had so far two hours and a half. So we allowed you four hours to cross-examine the witness, and it's apparent that it cannot be done by today. So I'm asking the parties whether -- and witness whether it would be agreeable to sit today for a limited time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It's certainly fine by the Prosecution, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic. Did I say what? Tomorrow, yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it it is in your -- yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can do it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it's no problem to proceed tomorrow. But I just want to indicate to you that I wouldn't be here because I have an interview in another city, that's been long planned, of a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it that would be in your interest as well, Mr. Turkusic, to sit tomorrow instead of continuing next week.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I was able to get the confirmation from the interpreters and court reporters that they can work for -- there's no logistical problem. That they can work, at the maximum, for two hours tomorrow, so we'll sit tomorrow at 10.00. We have five more minutes. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the last paragraph but one, you describe an aluminium part which you suppose served as a distance -- to fix the distance between the engines. Did you manage to reconstruct this part to establish how many engines there were?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: We didn't. We thought that unnecessary, and it was up to those who improvised and made the bomb. From everything else, it's clear that it's an improvised device that combined an air-bomb, that was supposed to be launched from a plane, dropped from a plane, with rocket engines of Grad type, and that's how they made this device for the purpose which we now see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the destructive effect in the street is minimal, and in this shallow crater there are four engines?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No. Show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's in the evidence. So since we are working tomorrow, we'll show it tomorrow. And tomorrow, then, with the kindness and the courtesy of the Trial Chamber and all the participants, we would deal with a number of other incidents in whose investigation you participated. Do you agree that, in that case, they did not provide you with enough elements, because you say this is a very destructive device?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: Where does it say which elements we were given and which we were not? You speak of the crater as an element. Information of that type is not given in the request that we were given. You can go back to page 1 and check.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you said it had huge destructive power?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct. That amount of explosive must have huge destructive power.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll look for that photograph in the evidence for tomorrow. Do you know that the Energoinvest factory "armatura" [phoen] was used during the war to cast casings for shells?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The first I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still have time to see 1D2171.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How far is this Energoinvest factory?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From your people. Do you know where that factory was located, and is it far from Safeta Zajke Street?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The factory Armature is somewhere in the same plane as the television building, and perhaps it's a couple kilometres away towards Drinska Street. I'm just guessing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it's close to the site of the incident. If it's between the television building and Drinska Street, it's very close to Safeta Zajke and Esad Midzic Street?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: No, you completely mixed up my answer. The factory of Armature is close to the television building if we look north-south. And if we look at Drinska Street, we have to go to the east, and that's where the distance is a couple of kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll have to go back to the map. Is this an interview with Berko Zecevic, who was some kind of manager in your military industry during the war?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I see the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at paragraph 7 on page 1?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: The first paragraph on page 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 7: "Austrians produce efficient mortar munitions from cast steel, which is not unlike munitions from a different type of steel. That must be done with special equipment which is high technology, and it was impossible in Sarajevo during the war. In Sarajevo, shells were made in Livnica at the casting -- the smelting factory in Alipasino Polje."

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC
utterances.text: I think you are reading sentences that are contradictory. It says it had to be done with special equipment, which was not possible in Sarajevo during the war. And then in Sarajevo, shells were made in a smelter in Alipasino Polje. If this person said these two things in one statement, then he is contradicting himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll stop here and continue tomorrow at 10.00. You should be able to -- you should finish your cross-examination in one and a half hours tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 5th day of November, 2010, at 10.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.02 p.m.,
